rationale: Final iteration, so this candidate races once for the score that counts most, and the goal is robustness on an unseen track of a different shape. The best raced design is iteration 7 (score 933.8). Iteration 9 (932.0) and iteration 8 (930.8) are within noise of it. Iteration 10 dropped to 911.8, mainly from the slalom (one off-track exit, progress 0.956), after wheel_track 0.10 m and kd 3.4 were combined. Iteration 8 showed that base_speed 1.0 added slalom instability without a clear time gain. Iteration 5 showed that kp 5.0 overcorrects at reversals. The oval and s-bend are saturated at about 950 and 945, so the remaining gap is slalom reliability at reversals. Iteration 7 has the most stable slalom at its wheel track (0.11 m, kd 3.0, base 0.95): 19/20 finished with 0 off-track exits and 0 line-loss events, and the single failure was a timeout, not a tape loss. I therefore reproduce iteration 7 exactly, with no untested changes, because the one-race budget cannot verify a new variant. The design is seven sensors at x = -0.04 to +0.04 m (0.0133 m pitch), weights 50*x, kp 4.5, ki 0, kd 3.0, base_speed 0.95, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.15 x 0.12 m, wheel track 0.11 m, radius 0.03 m, sensor size 0.012 m, and line_loss last_direction. Expected result: about 933 on the development tracks, with the oval and s-bend finishing 20/20 and the slalom finishing about 19/20. Hypotheses for the next (held-out) race: (1) if the unseen track's bends are sharper than the slalom, the limit is steering authority, and a narrower track or higher kp would help; (2) if completion_time is the main loss, base_speed 0.975 is the lever, at some risk of tape loss; (3) if off-track exits appear, kd should rise before speed changes. Measurements requested: all metrics, with focus on completion, completion_time and off-track versus timeout counts.
